data.title: Tesla Teases Next-Gen Roadster With Full-Width Light Bar Ahead of Reveal
data.description:
Tesla surprised viewers at the end of its Semi Rollout event in Nevada on Thursday night with a brief glimpse of its upcoming next-generation Roadster, offering the first look at what appears to be a significant design change ahead of its planned reveal next week.

The teaser arrived as a “one more thing” moment after Tesla wrapped up its Semi presentation. Before the clip played, Tesla engineering executive Lars Moravy told the audience, We can’t have a Semi event without the Roadster.”

The roughly nine-second video opens with the doors of a cargo trailer opening in darkness. A bright horizontal light bar then illuminates across the front of the vehicle, followed by flashes of Tesla and SpaceX branding before the glowing Roadster name appears on screen.

Tesla later shared the teaser on X from its official account with the caption “See you next week,” which lines up with the company’s planned next-generation Roadster reveal on October 1, 2026, in Waco, Texas.

The teaser provides another hint that Tesla is moving away from the original Roadster prototype design shown in 2017. That vehicle featured two separate curved headlights, while the new teaser appears to show a continuous front light bar stretching across the nose – a design element Tesla has introduced on vehicles including Cybertruck, Cybercab, Semi and the refreshed Model Y.

Tesla previously teased another view of the Roadster, showing a more angular rear design with a high-mounted wing and a wide taillight bar.

Tesla reopened Roadster reservations on September 18. Canadian customers are required to submit a $6,000 credit card payment listed as “Fully refundable,” followed by a $58,000 wire transfer due within 10 days. Tesla says, “Reservations are not final until the wire transfer payment is received.”

In the United States, the reservation process totals US$50,000, consisting of a US$5,000 card payment and US$45,000 wire transfer.

An upcoming temporary flight restriction over SpaceX’s McGregor, Texas test site has also drawn attention due to its proximity to the Waco reveal location, although the FAA notice does not mention Tesla or the Roadster. Tesla has previously confirmed the Roadster will be built in Texas.

data.title: EU vote on Tesla FSD slips beyond October
data.description:
Tesla’s hoped-for October vote on EU-wide approval of Full Self-Driving (FSD) is no longer on the agenda. The European Commission’s draft agenda for the October 6 meeting gives the Netherlands’ request a 25-minute discussion slot, but does not list a vote.

That pushes a decision to December at the earliest, assuming the matter is brought forward at a later meeting. However, the October agenda is still a draft, so it could still change.

The delay is disappointing for Tesla owners across Europe who hoped to use FSD this fall. The Netherlands approved FSD in April, and several other countries have since allowed its use. EU-wide approval, however, still requires a vote.

Tesla had pointed to October 6 as a possible date for the wider vote. The new agenda instead describes the item as a “continuation of discussions” on the Dutch request for authorization under Article 39. It offers no explanation for why a vote is absent or a confirmed date for one.

Regulators have been examining how the system handles issues such as speed limits and driver attention. France began its own on-road testing in September after it said it would not approve the system in its current form. That work gives the committee more to discuss, though the agenda does not say whether it caused the delay.

data.title: Tesla says Semi delivers 98% uptime as diesel costs soar
data.description:
Tesla is making its case for why trucking companies should switch from diesel to electric, highlighting lower energy costs, reduced maintenance, and more time on the road during its Semi Rollout event in Sparks, Nevada on Thursday evening.

With diesel prices in the US reaching record highs, Tesla believes the economics of its electric truck are becoming even more compelling, and the stats Tesla provided will make it difficult for fleet operators to ignore.

During the event, Tesla shared a chart titled “Electricity costs less than diesel,” comparing the cost per mile of a diesel truck averaging 7 mpg against the Semi consuming 1.7 kWh per mile.

According to Tesla’s chart, diesel costs have climbed from approximately $0.50 per mile earlier this year to more than $0.80 by September. Electricity, meanwhile, has remained relatively stable over the past 20 years at just above or below $0.20 per mile.

The comparison comes as US diesel prices have surged past $6.50 per gallon, nearly double their level a year ago.

Tesla also highlighted another important factor for commercial operators – keeping trucks moving. The company says its existing Semi fleet has achieved more than 98% uptime so far in 2026, compared to an industry average of approximately 90% to 95% for diesel Class 8 trucks.

Tesla claims the Semi “requires almost no maintenance,” with fewer mechanical components and a simplified drivetrain reducing the need for servicing.

To support customers, Tesla is developing a dedicated Semi service network, including mobile technicians, remote diagnostics, and over-the-air (OTA) software updates, just like its consumer fleet.

Tesla also plans to put its own trucks to work, confirming Semis will be used to transport freight between its facilities.

data.title: Tesla Reveals Major Semi Upgrades Including Electric Steering, New Heat Pump, and More
data.description:
Tesla officially inaugurated its Semi factory in Sparks, Nevada, on Thursday evening, revealing several previously undisclosed upgrades to its redesigned electric truck.

Beyond the exterior changes and efficiency improvements already announced, Tesla has made significant changes under the hood that should make the Semi cheaper to build, more efficient, and better suited for long-haul trucking.

One of the biggest changes is the Semi’s upgraded electric motors, which now feature a steel-caged rotor and bar-wound stator, sharing the same design found in the Cybertruck.

Another significant change is the introduction of fully electric steering. Tesla says the Semi is the first heavy-duty truck to eliminate hydraulic steering entirely, a move the company says lays the “groundwork for future autonomy.”

The redesigned Semi also introduces a new thermal management system called the Megamanifold, which uses a heat pump to manage temperatures in both the cabin and powertrain. Tesla says the same technology is used in the Cybercab.

This could be particularly beneficial for Canadian operators, where maintaining cabin comfort and battery temperatures during harsh winters can consume significant amounts of energy.

Inside the cab, Tesla has added acoustic glass to reduce road noise, along with a roll-down window, addressing a practical feature missing from earlier versions of the truck.

Drivers will also benefit from automated pre-trip inspections and integrated electronic logs (e-logs), helping simplify two routine but essential parts of commercial trucking.

Tesla also provided more detail about the switch from 2170 battery cells to their in-house 4680 cells. According to Tesla, the larger cells reduce the weight of the battery pack without sacrificing range, while also lowering production costs.

For a heavy-duty truck, reducing battery weight is particularly important. Every kilogram saved can potentially translate into additional payload capacity, making the Semi more competitive with traditional diesel trucks.

data.title: Tesla opens high-volume Semi factory in Nevada, hands over first keys to customers
data.description:
Tesla has officially launched high-volume production of the Semi at its dedicated factory in Sparks, Nevada. The milestone comes nearly nine years after the electric truck was first unveiled.

The announcement came during Tesla’s Semi Rollout event on Thursday evening, September 24, where the company began handing over keys to customers including PepsiCo, DHL and US Foods.

“Today, we’re launching high volume production,” Tesla Semi announced on X, adding that “Deliveries start now”.

Tesla has been delivering Semis to select customers since late 2022, but the opening of its dedicated factory marks the start of production on a much larger scale.

The new 1.8 million square foot factory has an annual production capacity of 50,000 trucks, with the Standard, Long Range and European-spec Semi all sharing the same assembly line.

Tesla is also bringing much of the manufacturing process in-house. Rather than simply assembling components from suppliers, the factory produces its own stampings, batteries, drive axles, high-voltage distribution systems, cooling modules and seats.

The Semi is also the first Class 8 truck to use a powder-coated finish.

The Standard Range Semi offers an estimated 325 miles (523 km) of range, while the Long Range version can travel 500 miles (805 km) on a charge when fully loaded. Tesla says customers have validated that longer figure in real-world operations, and that the truck can travel more than 600 miles (965 km) with lighter loads.

Tesla will also become a customer itself, using Semis to transport freight between its facilities.

However, the one big piece of information not revealed last night missing is the price of the Semi, although unofficial reports estimate the Standard Range at US$260,000 (C$352,000) and the Long Range at US$290,000 (C$392,500).

For Canada, the launch comes as R.R. Plett Trucking prepares to receive 12 Semis in June 2027, alongside plans for Megachargers in Langley and Kamloops. Meanwhile, Winnipeg-based Bison Transport is already testing the Semi with its drivers in the Chicago area.

You can watch the full presentation from last night’s Semi factory opening below.

data.title: Bentley Ditches 2030 All-Electric Target as they Launch the Bentley Torcal
data.description:
Bentley has decided to rethink the all-electric roadmap it announced in 2020 and has scrapped its plan to go all-electric by 2030.

According to the CEO, the change stems from market conditions, including declining demand for luxury EVs and shifting regulations in the automaker’s key jurisdictions.

The refreshed Beyond100+ Strategy will now see the car company target a full electric portfolio by 2035. The portfolio will keep plug-in hybrids on sale alongside EVs, including the newly launched Torcal, and shift output towards whatever powertrain customers are ordering.

The Torcal, with its 113-kWh battery and 800-volt architecture, should be the cornerstone of Bentley’s electric line-up for years to come. With a 600-km range and the ability to charge from 10% to 80% in 16 minutes, the Torcal and Torcal S both look to be high-performance luxury SUV’s that pack a punch.

The Torcal S is capable of 0-60 mph in as little as 2.8 seconds. The vehicle is a 2028 model and will go on sale next year in the United States and Europe.

In terms of what is coming down the line after the Torcal, Bentley has not said. However, many in the industry believe that Bentley will use a version of the Volkswagen Group’s SSP architecture rather than the Torcal’s Bentley-exclusive one. The SSP will allow eight different variants to be built on it, making it an ideal architecture for the automaker to build out a full line-up of vehicles for their key markets.

data.title: Tesla launches new Model 3/Y discounts in China
data.description:
Tesla has introduced a new round of discounts for Model 3 and Model Y buyers in China, with savings of up to 7,000 yuan (C$1,475/US$1,040) on the vehicles themselves.

For orders placed before October 31, the company will slash 5,000 yuan ($740) off any Model 3 variant. Tesla is pairing it with incentives such as 0% financing for up to five years. Buyers can also spend 8,000 yuan on the color option of their choice, and pick any of three charging perks.

The Model Y SUV also qualifies for a 7,000 yuan discount, with the same extras included.

Apart from the discounts mentioned above, Model 3 buyers also receive an 8,000 yuan insurance subsidy. The Performance All-Wheel Drive variant, however, is excluded from this particular benefit.

With all discounts combined, the Model 3 could drop to a starting price of 225,500 yuan, while the Model Y starts at 256,500 yuan.

Tesla, however, has another active promo with different eligibility requirements. For orders delivered before the end of September, the Model 3 qualifies for a 5,000 yuan discount, while the Model Y gets a 10,000 yuan rebate. Customers can not combine the two promos.

Tesla’s China sales have recently trended downward amid competition from local brands. August deliveries stood at 50,047 units, a 12.43 percent decline year-on-year. It was the third straight month of declining sales for the American company. In response, Tesla launched the fifth Model Y variant (Performance All-Wheel Drive) earlier this month.

data.title: Hyundai Ioniq 9 recalled after passengers injured by folding rear seats
data.description:
Hyundai is recalling 5,360 Ioniq 9 electric SUVs in the United States after discovering the electric SUV’s power-operated second-row seats may keep moving after they come into contact with a person or object.

The issue affects certain 2026 Ioniq 9s in Limited, Calligraphy and Calligraphy Design trims. When someone activates a powered function, including the automatic fold-and-stow feature, the seat may fail to detect an obstruction. That creates a risk of someone being trapped or injured, especially a child.

Hyundai told the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) it has received five complaints from U.S. owners, two of which alleged minor injuries. No recall has been issued by Transport Canada at the time of publication.

Hyundai began investigating the issue in March, and by August determined that certain second-row seats applied more force than the limits that had been set. The third-row systems tested below those limits.

For now, owners should check that nobody is sitting in or near the second-row seats before using the power-folding controls. Hyundai is particularly urging owners to keep children clear of the area while the seats move.

The fix is a change to the seat controller software. Dealers will inspect and update affected vehicles free of charge, while eligible owners who have opted in to Bluelink updates may receive the fix over the air (OTA).

data.title: Carney Says Canada Is Working to Cut Its Dependence on Starlink
data.description:
Canada is looking for ways to reduce its reliance on Starlink, according to Prime Minister Mark Carney. The move is part of a broader effort to give Canada more control over the technology it depends on, particularly for national security. 

In an interview with The New York Times, Carney acknowledged that other satellite networks do not yet match Starlink’s capabilities and resilience. He suggested that working with partners in Europe and potentially South Korea could help Canada build enough scale to reduce its dependence on the SpaceX system, particularly for defence communications. (via CultMTL)

Canada already has a domestic project underway. Ottawa has committed a $2.14-billion loan to Telesat Lightspeed, a planned low Earth orbit satellite network. The federal government has also secured capacity on Lightspeed for internet providers serving rural and remote areas. In Nunavut, Northwestel plans to use that capacity to connect communities across the territory.  

Despite Carney’s comments, that does not mean Canadians will be asked to give up the satellite internet service. Anyone can sign up for Starlink directly, but the comments are more directed to decisions governments make when they buy satellite service for their own operations or use public money to connect remote communities.

ALSO READ: Starlink Subscriber Count in Canada Tops 500,000

Quebec signed an agreement with SpaceX to bring Starlink to hard-to-reach households, covering equipment costs and part of the monthly bill for eligible customers.

Ontario planned a $100 million Starlink program for up to 15,000 underserved homes and businesses, but cancelled the partnership before it launched amid a tariff dispute earlier this year between Ontario Premier Doug Ford and U.S. President Donald Trump and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.

Similarly, Alberta offers eligible rural households a rebate toward satellite equipment. Nova Scotia has offered a rebate of up to $1,000 for setup costs through qualified satellite providers.

What happens next will depend on whether Canada can turn its plans into a reliable alternative. Telesat Lightspeed is expected to begin serving remote communities in the coming years, while Ottawa explores other options with international partners. Until those networks are ready, governments will still need to decide where Starlink remains the most practical way to keep people and essential services connected.

data.title: NHTSA investigates comma.ai after five crashes, three deaths
data.description:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) have opened an investigation into comma.ai. The investigation comes after several crashes, some of them fatal, in which vehicles equipped with the aftermarket driver assistance system reportedly struck stopped or slow-moving traffic in their lane.

What is comma.ai?

Comma.ai sells devices that drivers can add to compatible vehicles to provide sustained control of speed and steering. Its openpilot software uses cameras on the device alongside the vehicle’s existing sensors. Unlike a system installed by the automaker, the hardware is sold directly to consumers for installation in their own cars.

Comma.ai describes openpilot as capable of driving for extended periods without intervention, while stating that drivers must remain alert and prepared to take over at all times.

What is NHTSA investigating?

The NHTSA says that in all five crashes under review, vehicles fitted with comma.ai devices struck stopped or slow-moving vehicles ahead in the same lane.

Two crashes resulted in three deaths, while four caused injuries to 11 other people.

Investigators have so far confirmed the system was powered on or engaged in multiple incidents, but is still gathering data to determine its status in each crash. The agency is also investigating whether the system detected the vehicles ahead and how it responded before impact. 

The investigation covers the comma three, comma 3X and comma four devices, as well as openpilot. NHTSA estimates the affected population at 30,000 vehicles. Investigators will look at how the system handles stopped vehicles and other hazards in the travel lane, along with the safeguards meant to keep drivers attentive and ready to intervene.

The agency will also look at incidents involving modified versions of openpilot, known as forks.
